story: Founded in the early 1990s, Tract began as a small landscape architecture studio in Melbourne. Over the decades, we grew into a national practice known for creating sustainable, enduring, and memorable places. Our Southbank office sits at the heart of Melbourne's cultural and design hub, allowing us to collaborate with leading architects, developers, and communities.

We've shaped some of Australia's most iconic public spaces, from major urban renewal projects to intimate community gardens. Our team brings together landscape architects, town planners, urban designers, and media specialists who share a passion for placemaking. Every project is approached with creativity, rigour, and a deep respect for the local environment and culture.

Today, Tract operates from offices in Melbourne, Brisbane, Sydney, Geelong, Adelaide, and Sunshine Coast, but our roots remain in Southbank. We continue to push boundaries in sustainability, reconciliation, and climate resilience, ensuring the places we create today endure for future generations.

blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Landscape Design Cost in Southbank Melbourne 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Find out the average cost of landscape design in Southbank, Melbourne in 2026. From concept plans to full construction, we break down typical fees and what affects pricing.
body: If you're planning a landscape project in Southbank, Melbourne, one of the first questions you'll ask is 'how much does it cost?' In 2026, landscape design fees vary based on scope, site complexity, and the level of detail required. For a typical suburban garden in Southbank, a basic concept plan might start around $1,500, while a full design package with construction documentation can range from $5,000 to $15,000 depending on the size and features. Commercial projects scale higher, often exceeding $20,000 for comprehensive masterplans.

The cost of landscape design in Southbank is influenced by several factors unique to the area. The inner-city environment often requires careful consideration of drainage, heritage overlays, and council approvals. Sites with limited access or complex topography may need additional surveying and structural engineering input, which adds to the overall fee. Additionally, incorporating sustainable features like raingardens, permeable paving, and native planting can increase design time but offers long-term savings on water bills and maintenance.

Your choice of landscape architect also impacts the price. Established firms like Tract, with over 30 years of experience and a track record in Southbank and Melbourne, typically charge higher rates but deliver comprehensive services that include town planning liaison and council approvals. Freelance landscape designers may offer lower upfront costs but might not have the same depth of expertise in navigating local regulations. It's essential to compare quotes and check portfolios to ensure you're getting value for money.

Many clients in Southbank opt for a staged approach to manage costs. Start with a masterplan that outlines the overall vision, then phase the implementation over several years. This allows you to spread expenditure while ensuring a cohesive final outcome. Tract offers flexible packages from initial consultation ($0) through to full project management, so you can choose the level of involvement that suits your budget. We always provide fixed-price quotes upfront with no hidden surcharges.

In addition to design fees, you need to budget for council application costs in Southbank. The City of Melbourne may require a planning permit for significant changes like new structures, tree removal, or changes to levels. Application fees typically range from $200 to $1,500 depending on the project category. Tract's town planning specialists handle these applications as part of our service, saving you time and reducing the risk of refusal. We recommend including a contingency of 10-15% of the design fee for unexpected approvals costs.

Ultimately, investing in professional landscape design in Southbank pays off through increased property value, reduced maintenance, and a space that truly enhances your lifestyle. Homes with well-designed outdoor areas can see a 10-20% increase in resale value according to recent studies. By choosing a local practice like Tract, you ensure your design respects the unique character of Southbank while being functional and sustainable. Contact us for a free on-site consultation and a detailed quote tailored to your project.

blogPosts.title: Best Native Plants for Southbank Gardens — A 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the best native plants for Southbank gardens in 2026. Our guide covers drought-tolerant species, shade-loving shrubs, and ground covers that thrive in Melbourne's climate.
body: Southbank's urban microclimate presents both challenges and opportunities for gardeners. With its proximity to the Yarra River and dense built environment, temperatures can be a few degrees warmer than surrounding suburbs, but wind tunnelling between buildings can dry out soils. Choosing native plants that are adapted to Victoria's climate is a smart strategy for a low-maintenance, sustainable garden. In this guide, we share our top picks for native species that thrive in Southbank gardens in 2026.

For full-sun areas, consider Kangaroo Paw (Anigozanthos flavidus) which produces striking red and green flowers that attract birds. Another excellent choice is the Silver Banksia (Banksia marginata), a hardy shrub that copes well with wind and poor soil. Both species are drought-tolerant once established and require minimal watering. For ground cover, Native Violet (Viola hederacea) spreads quickly and thrives in semi-shade, making it perfect for underplanting beneath trees or along pathways.

In shaded spots typical of Southbank's courtyards and balconies, the Tassel Fern (Polystichum proliferum) adds lush greenery and texture. The Correa alba, or White Correa, produces delicate white flowers from autumn to spring and tolerates light frost. For a vertical accent, the Twining Glycine (Glycine clandestina) is a slender climber with purple pea flowers that won't overwhelm structures. These natives are not only beautiful but also support local biodiversity by providing food and habitat for insects and birds.

When designing a native garden in Southbank, think about layers: canopy, understorey, and ground cover. A small tree like the Eucalyptus leucoxylon 'Rosea' (Pink Flowering Yellow Gum) offers dappled shade and stunning winter blooms. Underneath, plant a mix of Dianella revolute (Flax Lily) and Lomatia myricoides (Long-leaf Lomatia) for year-round interest. Finally, use a mulch of locally sourced wood chips to retain moisture and suppress weeds. This layered approach mimics natural ecosystems and reduces maintenance.

Water management is crucial in Southbank's built environment. Native plants generally require less irrigation, but during establishment they need regular watering. Install a drip irrigation system on a timer to ensure efficient water use. Consider collecting rainwater from your roof for garden use — the City of Melbourne offers rebates for rainwater tanks. Tract's sustainable design team can integrate water-sensitive features into your garden layout, such as raingardens that filter stormwater runoff.

By choosing native plants for your Southbank garden, you create a space that is resilient, low-maintenance, and beautiful. Natives are perfectly adapted to Melbourne's variable rainfall and temperature extremes, and they attract local wildlife like bees, butterflies, and birds. Whether you're starting from scratch or refreshing an existing garden, our landscape architects can help you select the right species for your specific conditions. Contact Tract for a free consultation and let's bring your native garden vision to life.

blogPosts.title: Town Planning Permits in Southbank: What You Need to Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Navigating town planning permits in Southbank can be complex. Our guide explains when you need a permit, the application process, and how Tract's planners can help.
body: If you're planning any development in Southbank, whether a garden renovation, balcony addition, or new landscaping, you may need a town planning permit. The City of Melbourne has specific overlays that affect properties in Southbank, including heritage protections, flood zones, and design and development overlays. Understanding these regulations is crucial to avoid costly delays or fines. In this article, we break down what you need to know about town planning permits in Southbank in 2026.

When is a permit required? Common triggers include constructing a new structure over 1 metre high (e.g., pergolas, sheds, retaining walls), removing significant trees, changing ground levels, or installing hard surfaces that affect drainage. For apartment buildings, changes to common property or facade alterations often require permits. Even minor changes like installing a new fence or paving a courtyard can trigger permit requirements if located in a heritage overlay. Always check with a town planner before starting work.

The application process in Southbank typically involves submitting detailed plans, a written report, and supporting documentation to the City of Melbourne. The council assesses the proposal against the planning scheme, overlays, and neighbourhood character. The process can take 4-12 weeks depending on complexity and whether public notification is required. Tract's town planning team has extensive experience with Southbank applications and can prepare all documentation to maximise approval chances on the first submission.

One common issue in Southbank is the requirement for a Landscape Plan as part of a planning application. This plan must show existing and proposed vegetation, hard surfaces, drainage, and lighting. Our in-house landscape architects create these plans seamlessly, ensuring compliance with council requirements. We also handle consultation with neighbours if required, which can be a sensitive part of the process. By managing the entire planning application, we save you time and stress.

The cost of a town planning permit application in Southbank varies. Council fees range from $300 to $1,500 depending on the project value. However, professional fees for preparing plans, reports, and managing the application can range from $2,000 to $10,000. While this may seem like an expense, it is a fraction of the cost of retrospective approval or enforcement action. Tract offers fixed-price packages for permit applications so you know exactly what you're paying upfront.

If you're unsure whether your Southbank project needs a permit, the safest approach is to get a professional assessment. Tract offers a free initial consultation where we review your site and proposed works, advise on permit pathways, and provide a cost estimate for our services. We have a strong track record of successful approvals across Melbourne, including many in Southbank's sensitive heritage areas. Contact us today to get started with confidence.

blogPosts.title: Sustainable Urban Design Trends in Southbank 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Explore the top sustainable urban design trends shaping Southbank in 2026, from green roofs and rain gardens to shared streets and biodiversity corridors.
body: Southbank is at the forefront of sustainable urban design in Melbourne, driven by its dense urban fabric, high-rise living, and proximity to the Yarra River. In 2026, several trends are reshaping how we design public and private spaces in this dynamic neighbourhood. From green infrastructure to inclusive placemaking, these approaches not only improve environmental outcomes but also enhance quality of life for residents and visitors. Here's what's trending in Southbank urban design.

Green roofs and vertical gardens continue to gain popularity in Southbank. New developments are required to include green cover to mitigate the urban heat island effect and improve stormwater management. We're seeing innovative designs that integrate edible gardens, native plantings, and even small trees on rooftops. These spaces provide residents with private outdoor areas, while reducing building energy consumption. Tract has designed several award-winning green roofs in Southbank, combining aesthetics with ecology.

Rain gardens and water-sensitive urban design (WSUD) are now standard in Southbank streetscape projects. These features capture stormwater runoff, filter pollutants, and recharge groundwater, while adding visual interest. The City of Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy encourages permeable paving, swales, and bioretention basins. In private developments, we incorporate raingardens into courtyards and plazas to manage water on-site. This approach reduces pressure on the drainage system and creates lush microclimates.

Shared streets and pedestrian-priority zones are transforming Southbank's laneways. By removing kerbs and using textured paving, these streets slow traffic and encourage walking and cycling. Planters, seating, and public art activate these spaces, making them desirable destinations. Tract's urban designers work with communities to co-create these shared spaces, ensuring they reflect local identity. The success of Southbank's shared streets has inspired similar projects across Melbourne.

Biodiversity corridors are also a key focus. Southbank's location along the Yarra River makes it an important link for wildlife movement. New developments are incorporating native vegetation corridors that connect parks and riparian zones. Planting locally indigenous species supports local birds, bees, and beneficial insects. Tract's landscape architects specialise in creating biodiverse planting plans that enhance ecological connectivity while maintaining a refined aesthetic suitable for urban settings.

As we move further into 2026, the demand for sustainable urban design in Southbank will only increase. Residents expect their buildings and public spaces to contribute positively to the environment and their wellbeing. By investing in green infrastructure, active transport, and community-focused design, Southbank can remain a model of sustainable urban living. Tract is proud to be part of this movement. If you're planning a development in Southbank, contact us to explore how sustainable design can add value to your project.
